body.heading: New is a vulnerable country
paragraphs: New job, new school, new neighbourhood, new country — the details differ, the feeling is the same: everyone else knows the routines, the jokes, and where things are, and you know none of it.
In that state, small signals carry enormous weight. One person who explains the unwritten rules or saves you a seat can change how a whole place feels.

body.heading: A welcome in three moves
paragraphs: First, introduce yourself before they have to — being approached is far easier than approaching. Second, explain one unwritten rule: 'We always order lunch on Fridays; join us.' Third, follow up once next week. A single invitation can be politeness; a second one is belonging.
You will not always become friends, and that is fine. You were the person who made the door feel open, and they will remember it when they are the established one.

description: Everyone remembers being the new person. Being welcomed well is a small thing you never forget — and easy to give.
